scenes.anchor_text:
“Above silence, the illuminating storms—dying storms— illuminate the silence above.”
The above sample is noteworthy as it is a ketek, a complex form of holy Vorin poem.
scenes.scene_description: A vast, roiling stormscape fills the sky, punctuated by intense, dying lightning strikes. The storm illuminates a lower layer of ethereal silence, and above, another expanse of quietude, creating a sense of immense scale and mystery.

scenes.anchor_text: The fact that this one was uttered by an illiterate, dying Herdazian in a language he barely spoke should be of particular note. There is no record of this particular ketek in any repository of Vorin poetry, so it is very unlikely that the subject was merely repeating something he once heard.
scenes.scene_description: A dimly lit, cavernous chamber with Vorin scholars poring over ancient texts. The Herdazian is shown as a frail, dying figure in the background as they attempt to decipher something he is about to say.

scenes.anchor_text: We leave it to His Majesty’s mind, on a strong day, to puzzle out the meaning of why the storms might be important, and what the poem may mean by indicating that there is silence both above and below said storms.
scenes.scene_description: A serene royal study overlooking a storm-swept landscape. A massive window offers a panoramic view of the tumultuous skies, hinting at the deeper mysteries the king must contemplate.
